subject: ela
skillName: Identify different story points of view

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara and James both looked at the same painting at the art museum. Amara said, "It looks like a peaceful garden." James said, "It looks messy and confusing."

How do Amara and James feel differently about the same painting?
items.answer: Amara thinks the painting is peaceful and relaxing. James thinks it looks messy and confusing. They have different feelings about the same artwork.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia's family got a new puppy. Sofia thought it was the best day of her life. Her cat, however, hissed and hid under the bed.

How does the new puppy look different to Sofia and to the cat?
items.answer: Sofia is thrilled about the new puppy. The cat is afraid or upset and hides. The same puppy is exciting for Sofia and frightening for the cat.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo and his dad went to a baseball game. Leo's dad loved every slow, quiet moment between pitches. Leo kept asking, "When will someone hit a home run?"

How do Leo and his dad feel differently about the pace of the baseball game?
items.answer: Leo's dad enjoys the slow, quiet moments of the game. Leo finds them boring and wants more action. They have different points of view about what makes baseball enjoyable.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia's teacher gave the class extra homework to practice for the test. Most students groaned. Nadia said, "Good — I needed more practice."

How is Nadia's point of view on the extra homework different from her classmates'?
items.answer: Most students are unhappy about the extra homework. Nadia welcomes it because she knows she needs more practice. Her point of view is more positive than her classmates'.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Owen and his sister found a big, empty box. Owen said, "We can make a spaceship!" His sister said, "I want to make a house."

How does Owen's point of view differ from his sister's about what to do with the box?
items.answer: Owen wants to make a spaceship. His sister wants to make a house. They both see the same box but have different ideas about what it can become.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara thought the cafeteria pizza was delicious. Her friend Jade thought it tasted like cardboard. They both had the same pizza for lunch.

How do Amara and Jade feel differently about the pizza?
items.answer: Amara thinks the pizza is delicious. Jade thinks it tastes like cardboard. They ate the same food but have completely different opinions about it.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo's dad said it was time to clean the garage. Leo thought it sounded boring. Then his dad pulled out Leo's old baby photos, a stack of comic books, and a broken remote-control car that could be fixed. Leo changed his mind.

How did Leo's point of view about cleaning the garage change?
items.answer: At first Leo thought cleaning the garage would be boring. When he discovered old photos, comic books, and a fixable car, he changed his mind and became interested.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia's grandmother visited and watched Sofia do homework on a tablet. "When I was your age, we had to write everything by hand," her grandmother said. "That sounds exhausting," said Sofia.

How does Sofia's point of view differ from her grandmother's about doing schoolwork?
items.answer: Sofia's grandmother remembers writing everything by hand as normal. Sofia thinks it sounds exhausting. Their different points of view come from growing up in different times.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James wanted to stay up late on a school night to finish his book. His mom said bedtime was bedtime, no exceptions. James thought it was unfair. His mom said sleep was more important than finishing a story.

How does James's point of view differ from his mom's?
items.answer: James thinks staying up to finish his book is worth it. His mom thinks getting enough sleep is more important. They have different priorities for the same evening.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia saw a spider in the corner of the classroom. She was fascinated and moved closer to look. Her friend Marcus screamed and jumped on his chair.

How do Nadia and Marcus feel differently about the same spider?
items.answer: Nadia is fascinated by the spider and wants to look closer. Marcus is afraid and jumps on his chair. The same spider causes curiosity in one person and fear in the other.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Owen's family was getting a new baby sister. Owen's parents were so happy they could not stop smiling. Owen had a plan to teach her how to ride a bike. His cat was unimpressed and went to sleep.

How does each character in this story feel about the new baby?
items.answer: Owen's parents are joyful and excited. Owen is eager and has plans for activities with her. The cat does not care at all and goes to sleep. All three have different reactions to the same news.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara practiced the violin for thirty minutes every day. Her neighbor knocked on the door to ask if she could practice more quietly. Amara felt proud of her progress. Her neighbor felt the sound was too loud.

What is Amara's point of view on her violin practice? What is her neighbor's point of view?
items.answer: Amara feels proud and sees practice as progress. Her neighbor is bothered by the noise. They have different points of view about the same violin playing.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo's little cousin came to visit. He thought Leo's room was the coolest place he had ever been. Leo had not cleaned it in weeks and was embarrassed.

How do Leo and his cousin feel differently about Leo's room?
items.answer: Leo's cousin thinks the room is amazing. Leo is embarrassed because it is messy. They see the same room very differently.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia got to school early and the playground was empty and quiet. She thought it felt peaceful. Her friend Jade arrived later and said, "I hate when it's this quiet. It feels lonely."

How do Sofia and Jade feel differently about the quiet playground?
items.answer: Sofia finds the quiet peaceful. Jade finds it lonely. The same empty playground gives each person a completely different feeling.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James watched his baby sister take her first steps. She fell down twice but got back up each time. James cheered. His sister seemed surprised by all the fuss and toddled toward the dog instead.

How do James and his sister feel about the same moment?
items.answer: James is excited and proud of his sister's first steps. His baby sister is not aware of the big deal — she is just moving toward the dog. James sees a milestone; his sister just sees a dog to walk toward.
